newsitem.title: USA: Mother Teresa 'miracle' bun draws Nashville crowds.
newsitem.headline: Mother Teresa 'miracle' bun draws Nashville crowds.

text.p: Hundreds of people have flocked to a small Nashville coffee shop to see a "miraculous" likeness of Mother Teresa -- on a cinnamon bun.

Visitors were lining up at the Bongo Java coffee shop on Saturday to stare at the bun, which was glazed and put on display in a glass cabinet after a customer who bought it remarked how its shape looked like the Roman Catholic missionary.

The cinnamon bun is said to bear an amazing likeness to the nun's face, complete with her head covering. Most customers smile at the sight, but some regard it as a genuine miracle, said coffee shop owner Bob Bernstein.
"It started out as a fun thing," said Bernstein, "but it's attracting an awful lot of attention."
"Yes, that's Mother Teresa all right," one customer said on Saturday.
The bun was made on Oct. 15 and local musician Ryan Finney was about to take a bite when he noted the uncanny resemblance.
"I almost ate it," he said. The staff decided to preserve it, and a young Nashville filmmaker even made a short movie that reportedly has sold 100 copies.

Shop manager Ann Loree says the staff have a lot of fun with their hard work and "we think that spirit is why we were chosen for the Mother Teresa cinnamon bun." They plan to put a picture of the bun on the Internet.
Quoting a saying by Mother Teresa, the Nobel Peace Prize winner who is recovering at her home in India from heart surgery, Loree said: "Where there is great love, there are always great miracles."
